title: Jug bands before and after McDonald
summary: Allen and Jasper Taylor ask about earlier jug bands. Jones says only McDonald got fine jobs, including the Hippodrome in New York, before coming to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: He was the first one around those all. He was the original Jug Blower. Did you ever encounter, Jasper, did you ever encounter jug bands before 20? Well, yes, I saw the original across the street from the barbershop. I played over there. Well, was it this group or another? It was this group. Not Grandy. Yeah. I knew Grandy. He played. All right. Grandy came later. He also played jug. But I wondered if there were other jug bands before this thing started in Louisville. Now, in Louisville there were several jugs blowing after a while. But had you heard of any in 1915 or 16 or anywhere? The Louisville Jug Band was my first one. First encounter. I haven't heard of a jug down in New Orleans, but I wonder if it could have started around Louisville that's effect out of a jug. Do you play that?

That's the only one that I know of is Earl McDonnell. I know several that come up after he did, but I never did pay any attention to them, because they weren't the rich one, and they didn't get no jobs in the first beginning. They never was put out or hired for no fine jobs and things like that. But Earl, he showed the Hippodrome, New York, and all the biggest, finest places you could find. He wasn't hired. And when we came here to Chicago in 20, we was hired by Jack Rees. Jack Rees had a cabaret at Ohio on State Street, classic cabaret.
